explain.say: A junction has to let traffic from different roads cross safely. Two common answers are the roundabout and the set of traffic lights.

explain.say: At a roundabout, drivers give way to traffic already circling, then join when there is a gap. Nobody waits at a red light on an empty road, so in light or balanced traffic it keeps everything moving.

explain.say: Traffic lights give each direction a turn. That wastes time when roads are quiet, but when one road is very busy, lights make sure side roads and pedestrians still get a fair chance to go.

explain.say: Roundabouts are safer in one important way: cars must slow down and can only meet at shallow angles, not head-on or side-on. Many busy roundabouts add traffic lights to get the best of both.

faq.q: Who has priority at a roundabout?
faq.a: In the UK you give way to traffic coming from your right, already on the roundabout. In countries that drive on the right, you give way to traffic from the left.
asks: Do you give way to the right at a roundabout?

faq.q: Why are roundabouts safer than crossroads?
faq.a: Drivers have to slow down to go round, and paths only cross at shallow angles, so the worst head-on and side-on crashes are almost impossible. Studies find far fewer injury crashes after crossroads become roundabouts.

faq.q: When are traffic lights better than a roundabout?
faq.a: When one road is much busier, its steady stream can leave no gaps for side roads at a roundabout. Lights share the time fairly and give safe crossings for pedestrians and cyclists.
asks: Why use traffic lights instead of a roundabout?

faq.q: Why do some roundabouts have traffic lights?
faq.a: At very busy roundabouts, lights on the entries control the flow so no road is blocked for long. It combines the roundabout's flow with the fairness of lights.
asks: Why are there lights on a roundabout?

faq.a: A mini roundabout is a painted circle or small dome that drivers go round or over. It follows the same give-way rules but fits a small junction.
asks: How do you use a mini roundabout?

facts: The rule that traffic on a roundabout has priority was introduced in the UK in 1966.
Swindon's Magic Roundabout is made of five mini roundabouts arranged around a central one.
US studies found that converting crossroads to roundabouts cut injury crashes by about 75 percent.
